page: UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-32GB is a compute-focused cloud server instance featuring 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with one thread per core, the processor includes modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic accelerators. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core, and includes 300 GB of bundled local SSD storage along with one complimentary public IPv4 address. It operates without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core execution alongside balanced multi-threaded capacity. The server achieves top-tier results in single-threaded workloads, recording 2,283.0 on Geekbench single-core and 3,712.18 on stress-ng single-core tests. High performance is further sustained in data manipulation pipelines, with single-threaded compression reaching 41.85 GB/sec on gzip and 16.97 GB/sec on bzip3 decompression. Aggregate multi-core metrics, including Geekbench multi-core (14,885.0), stress-ng multi-core (40,603.39), and PassMark CPU score (32,030.94), fall within the middle 50% tier. In-memory throughput and cache performance remain stable, delivering 28.62 million Redis SET operations per second and 16.46 GB/sec in static web serving.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio establishes high compute density at a qualitative cost efficiency advantage over memory-heavy configurations. However, workloads requiring intensive multi-token LLM inference or massive RAM footprints may encounter bottlenecks, as indicated by bottom-tier performance in small model LLM text generation (13.21 tokens/sec). UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-32GB is well aligned for compilation pipelines, batch compression tasks, microservice hosting, CI/CD runners, and compute-heavy API backends requiring robust per-thread execution.
